exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.anatomy_pov: The latissimus dorsi originates from your lower spine and iliac crest, inserting at the humerus. Vertical pulling stretches these fibers fully, heavily recruiting the teres major to physically flare your upper back outward for the V-taper.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rows
exercises.anatomy_pov: Targets the rhomboids (major and minor) and the middle fibers of the trapezius. Horizontally retracting the scapula thickens the mid-back musculature, pulling your shoulders back and preventing a flat side profile.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldowns
exercises.anatomy_pov: Pure shoulder extension. This isolates the lower lats without engaging the biceps. It forces the serratus anterior to engage, creating those defined 'rib' muscles under your chest.

exercises.name: Bicep Curls
exercises.anatomy_pov: The biceps brachii has two heads (short and long) originating at the scapula. Because compound pulls pre-exhaust them, this pure elbow flexion forces localized hypertrophy to build the 'peak'.

optional_exercises.name: Hammer Curls
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: A neutral grip shifts the load to the brachialis (the muscle underneath the bicep) and the brachioradialis. Growing these literally pushes the bicep up, making the arm look 3D.

optional_exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrugs
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: Isolates the descending (upper) fibers of the trapezius muscle, creating a thick, muscular transition from the shoulders to the neck.

finisher.name: Mountain Climbers
finisher.anatomy_pov: A dynamic plank that spikes the heart rate. Driving the knees engages the lower rectus abdominis, while stabilizing the shifting weight heavily taxes the internal and external obliques.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.anatomy_pov: The pec major has two main heads. Flat pressing primarily loads the massive sternocostal head (originating at the sternum), dragging the humerus horizontally to build overall chest density.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.anatomy_pov: The incline shifts tension to the clavicular (upper) head of the pec, which originates at the collarbone. Fleshing this out creates a thick 'shelf' that visually connects the chest to the front shoulders.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Crossovers
exercises.anatomy_pov: Takes the chest through its full range of motion. The downward angle explicitly targets the lower (abdominal) fibers of the pec major, creating that sharp, defined line at the bottom of the chest.

exercises.name: Tricep Extensions
exercises.anatomy_pov: The triceps make up 2/3 of upper arm mass. Pushing downward isolates the lateral and medial heads through pure elbow extension without shoulder involvement.

optional_exercises.name: Pec Deck Flyes
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: A strict isolation movement. Because the arms stay slightly bent, the chest is forced to do 100% of the horizontal adduction, stretching the muscle fibers maximally at the bottom.

optional_exercises.name: Dips
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: A heavy compound bodyweight push that simultaneously hits the lower pecs, the front delts, and all three heads of the triceps.

finisher.name: Bicycle Crunches
finisher.anatomy_pov: The rotational movement explicitly targets the external obliques. Compressing the sides of your waist forces the muscle to tighten, acting directly against love handles.

exercises.name: Squats
exercises.anatomy_pov: Systemic CNS engagement. The descent loads the gluteus maximus and hamstrings, while the concentric push relies heavily on all 4 heads of the quadriceps to extend the knee and hip simultaneously.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlifts (RDLs)
exercises.anatomy_pov: A pure hip-hinge. By keeping the knees slightly bent but fixed, it places extreme stretch-mediated tension on the biceps femoris and semitendinosus (hamstrings), forcing massive growth.

exercises.name: Leg Curls
exercises.anatomy_pov: Whereas RDLs work the hamstrings at the hip, leg curls isolate them at the knee joint. This dual-joint training prevents muscle imbalances caused by quad-heavy pressing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lunges
exercises.anatomy_pov: Unilateral hip extension. Forces the gluteus medius and minimus to fire aggressively just to keep you balanced, while deeply stretching the trailing leg's hip flexors.

optional_exercises.name: Calf Raises
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: Standing calf raises lock the knee, perfectly isolating the gastrocnemius (the upper, visible diamond-shaped calf muscle) through plantar flexion.

optional_exercises.name: Leg Extensions
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: Pure isolation for the quadriceps. Specifically targets the rectus femoris, which crosses both the hip and the knee, creating deep cuts in the front of the thigh.

finisher.name: Side Plank Hip Dips
finisher.anatomy_pov: Isometrically loads the quadratus lumborum and the obliques. Lowering and raising the hips creates massive tension on the lateral core wall, shrinking the love handle silhouette.

schedule_2.notes: Focus on mobility work, stretching, and hitting daily protein goals to repair tissue.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.anatomy_pov: The deltoid has 3 heads. Vertical pressing heavily taxes the anterior (front) head originating from the clavicle, and the lateral (side) head, building raw boulder-shoulder mass.

exercises.name: Lateral Raises
exercises.anatomy_pov: Because the front and rear heads are mechanically disadvantaged here, the lateral (side) head takes 100% of the load. This is the single most important exercise for widening your V-taper frame.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.anatomy_pov: Isolates the posterior (rear) head of the deltoid originating on the spine of the scapula. Growing this pulls your shoulders backward, fixing posture and completing the 3D shoulder look.

exercises.name: Russian Twists
exercises.anatomy_pov: The transverse abdominis holds the torso steady while the internal and external obliques execute spinal rotation, actively tightening the muscular sheath around the waistline.

optional_exercises.name: Upright Rows
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: A compound pull that recruits the lateral deltoids and the upper trapezius simultaneously, bridging the gap between shoulder and neck musculature.

optional_exercises.name: Front Raises
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: Strict isolation for the anterior deltoid. Fleshing this out makes the shoulder pop from a side-profile view.

finisher.name: Heel Touches (Penguin Crunches)
finisher.anatomy_pov: Creates lateral flexion of the spine. By reaching side to side, you force the obliques into a hard concentric contraction, literally squeezing the fat stores at the love handles.

exercises.name: Deadlifts
exercises.anatomy_pov: The ultimate posterior hinge. The erector spinae (lower back) stabilizes the spine, while the gluteus maximus and hamstrings fire to lock out the hips. The isometric grip taxes the lats and traps.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldowns
exercises.anatomy_pov: A secondary weekly volume hit to the lats. Using a wider grip specifically isolates the upper/outer sweeping fibers of the latissimus dorsi.

exercises.name: T-Bar Rows
exercises.anatomy_pov: A heavy horizontal pull. The neutral grip allows for maximal scapular retraction, packing dense, thick muscle onto the middle/lower traps and rhomboids.

exercises.name: Face Pulls
exercises.anatomy_pov: Targets the often-neglected external rotators of the rotator cuff (infraspinatus and teres minor) alongside the rear delts, bulletproofing the shoulders against bench-press injuries.

optional_exercises.name: Hyperextensions
optional_exercises.anatomy_pov: Isolates the erector spinae. Strengthening the lower back muscles prevents rounding during heavy squats and deadlifts, keeping your spine safe.

finisher.name: Cable Woodchoppers
finisher.anatomy_pov: A transverse-plane movement that mimics athletic rotation. It diagonally loads the obliques under heavy resistance, carving deep V-lines into the lower abdomen.

schedule_2.notes: Let the central nervous system recover. Hydrate heavily and prep meals for the week.
